## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

⚠️ **Gate recommendation: approve with a non-blocking risk.**

The observed-key union preserves later fields in ordinary dictionary writes and keeps columns omitted from the whole batch absent for partial merge updates. Local add, create, merge, and boundary checks pass.

Blob rows retain the existing field-loss limitation. [#4485](https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb/pull/4485) is an earlier open fix for the same issue that also covers blob conversion; coordinate which implementation lands.

⚠️ **Gate recommendation: approve with a non-blocking risk.**

Ordinary dictionary writes preserve later fields, and columns omitted from the whole batch remain absent for partial merge updates. The targeted tests and sync/async ingestion checks pass with the updated dependencies.

The [previously reported blob-row limitation](https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb/pull/4813#discussion_r4455649438) remains unchanged: later ordinary fields can still be lost during blob conversion. Including nullable keys in the first row avoids that loss. [#4485](https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb/pull/4485) remains an earlier open alternative that also covers blob rows.

⚠️ **Gate recommendation: approve with a non-blocking risk.**

Ordinary dictionary writes retain fields first seen in later rows, while partial merges preserve columns omitted from the whole batch. Targeted regression and sync/async ingestion checks pass on this revision.

The [blob-row limitation](https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb/pull/4813#discussion_r4455649438) is unchanged: later ordinary fields can still be lost during blob conversion. Supplying nullable keys in the first row avoids the loss. [#4485](https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb/pull/4485) remains an open alternative covering blob conversion as well.

With an explicit `note: string not null` field, `create_table` rejects `[{"id": 1}, {"id": 2, "note": "new"}]` on the base. On this revision it succeeds, stores null for the first row, and reopens with `note` marked nullable. Later appends can then omit `note` too.

Please preserve the supplied field’s nullability during schema alignment. A regression test should reject the missing non-null value and check that a valid create still has a non-nullable `note` after reopen. Missing nullable fields and columns omitted from an entire partial-update batch should keep their current behavior.

⚠️ **Gate recommendation: approve with a non-blocking risk.**

Verified the [author’s update](https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb/pull/4813#issuecomment-7212836780): `create_table` now rejects the reported missing non-nullable `note` value, and a valid create preserves that constraint after reopening. Ordinary dictionary writes retain later fields, and partial merges preserve columns omitted from the whole batch.

Primitive fixed-size-list children still follow Lance’s existing [schema normalization](https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb/pull/5036): their child field reopens as nullable. Preserving the input flag during alignment does not make that child constraint durable.

The [blob-row limitation](https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb/pull/4813#discussion_r4455649438) also remains unchanged: later ordinary fields can still disappear during blob conversion. Including nullable keys in the first row avoids that loss; [#4485](https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb/pull/4485) remains an open alternative covering blob conversion.

Thanks for fixing the top-level `note` constraint. A missing value is now rejected, and a valid table keeps `note` non-nullable after reopen.

`3539268b` also rejects a valid null parent. Build an Arrow table from `[{"profile": {"country": "CN"}}, {"profile": None}]`, write and read it with `pyarrow.parquet`, then call `create_table` with an explicit nullable `profile` struct whose `country` field is `string not null`. The Parquet reader returns a null child slot beneath the null `profile`. The base and previous head write and reopen both rows. On this revision the Arrow cast rejects the masked slot before the native writer runs.

Please preserve the child constraint in the stored schema and enforce it only where `profile` is present. A regression test should round-trip the null `profile` case and reject a present `profile` with a null `country`.

⚠️ **Gate recommendation: approve with a non-blocking risk.**

Verified the [author’s update](https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb/pull/4813#issuecomment-7214498436): the Parquet `profile: null` case now round-trips with `country` still non-nullable, while a present profile with a null country is rejected. Later dictionary fields and partial merges retain their intended behavior.

Map values remain an exception to the parent-mask handling; rebuilding the Arrow input with the explicit schema is a verified workaround. Primitive fixed-size-list children also retain Lance’s existing [schema normalization](https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb/pull/5036), reopening as nullable.

The [blob-row limitation](https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb/pull/4813#discussion_r4455649438) remains unchanged: later ordinary fields can disappear during blob conversion. Including nullable keys in the first row avoids that loss; [#4485](https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb/pull/4485) remains an open alternative covering blob conversion.

review_comments.body:
Rows with blob fields still bypass the new helper, so an ordinary field first supplied in a later row is silently lost. `_blob_input_to_arrow` builds its table with `pa.Table.from_pylist(rows)` before returning here; the ordinary `add` path also calls that conversion first. This behavior is unchanged from the base, but those inputs do not receive this fix.

Including the nullable key in the first row (with `None` if needed) avoids the loss. The shared conversion in [#4485](https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb/pull/4485) covers this path as well.

<details>
<summary>Reproducer</summary>

```python
import lancedb
import pyarrow as pa

db = lancedb.connect("memory://")
schema = pa.schema([
    pa.field("id", pa.int64()),
    pa.field("note", pa.string()),
    lancedb.blob("payload"),
])
table = db.create_table("example", schema=schema)
table.add([
    {"id": 1, "payload": b"a"},
    {"id": 2, "payload": b"b", "note": "keep me"},
])
assert table.to_arrow()["note"].to_pylist() == [None, "keep me"]
# Observed on this head: [None, None]
```

</details>

Nullable struct values inside maps still reject valid Parquet input. This cast reinstates the original non-nullable child fields before the null map/item parents are filtered, so a masked `country` slot raises the same Arrow error. The base accepts and reopens these rows. Keeping the relaxed type while extracting map items, then validating only present parents, would cover this boundary.

This fails visibly before creating the table; rebuilding the input with `pa.Table.from_pylist(source.to_pylist(), schema=schema)` permits a same-name retry and preserves the stored child constraint.

<details>
<summary>Reproducer</summary>

```python
import tempfile
import lancedb
import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

country = pa.struct([pa.field("country", pa.string(), nullable=False)])
schema = pa.schema([pa.field("profile", pa.map_(pa.string(), country))])
source = pa.table({
    "profile": pa.array(
        [[("a", {"country": "CN"})], [("b", None)]],
        type=pa.map_(pa.string(), pa.struct([pa.field("country", pa.string())])),
    )
})
buffer = pa.BufferOutputStream()
pq.write_table(source, buffer)
source = pq.read_table(pa.BufferReader(buffer.getvalue()))
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as path:
    db = lancedb.connect(path)
    table = db.create_table("test", data=source, schema=schema)
    assert table.to_arrow().to_pylist() == source.to_pylist()
```

Expected: both rows round-trip. Observed: `RuntimeError` containing `field 'country' of type string has nulls. Can't cast to non-nullable field 'country' of type string`.

</details>

comments.body:
Fixed: schema alignment no longer relaxes a field declared non-nullable (inferred input fields are always nullable, and that flag was being copied over). `create_table` now rejects the missing value with "Casting field 'note' with null values to non-nullable", and a valid create keeps `note` non-nullable after reopen; the new test covers both. This applies to nested children too, while missing nullable fields and columns omitted from a whole partial-update batch behave as before.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

Fixed: a null `profile` now round-trips through `create_table`, `country` stays non-nullable in the stored schema, and a present `profile` with a null `country` is rejected. Arrow's cast checks child slots regardless of the parent, so struct children are now checked separately, only where the parent is present. The new test covers the Parquet round trip and the rejection.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
